sections.Astrophysical Alerts:
#### PKS 0521−365: H.E.S.S. reports a >10σ very-high-energy detection during the gamma-ray high state

H.E.S.S. reported on **17 November 2026 at 18:19 UTC** that it detected the radio-loud active galaxy **PKS 0521−365** at very high energies. The array observed for about **3.5 h during the night of 16–17 November** after a Fermi-LAT high-state alert; its preliminary onsite analysis gives a detection significance **above 10σ**. The source is at **RA 05h 22m 57.98s, Dec −36° 27′ 30.85″** and redshift **z = 0.057**. [H.E.S.S. report](https://www.astronomerstelegram.org/?read=18157); [preceding Fermi-LAT alert](https://www.astronomerstelegram.org/?read=18134).

The telegram supplies neither a very-high-energy flux nor a spectrum, and the quoted significance comes from a rapid onsite analysis. It therefore establishes a strong preliminary VHE detection, not yet a calibrated spectral result. The earlier Fermi-LAT alert concerned a historical GeV maximum on 22 October; the H.E.S.S. observation shows that elevated high-energy activity remained scientifically productive weeks later, but contemporaneous light curves are needed before claiming a direct GeV–TeV correlation.

#### EP261115a: refined WXT data reveal an ≳80-s hard X-ray transient

Einstein Probe refined its analysis of **EP261115a** in a circular issued **17 November at 06:39 UTC**. The WXT event began at **2026-11-15 00:20:57 UTC**, about 76 s earlier than the original trigger time, and remained active for at least **about 80 s** before the light curve was interrupted by the spacecraft's autonomous follow-up. [Refined WXT analysis](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46312); [event group](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/events/ep261115a).

For the time-averaged 0.5–4 keV spectrum, the team fitted an absorbed power law with Galactic \(N_{\rm H}\) fixed at **1.0 × 10²⁰ cm⁻²**. It obtained photon index **0.48 ± 0.53** and average unabsorbed flux **7.30⁺²·⁶⁴₋₂·₀₄ × 10⁻¹⁰ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻²**. The unusually hard best-fit index is imprecise, and the absorption column was fixed rather than inferred. FXT analysis was still pending, while the optical follow-ups reported previously provided only upper limits. The event is therefore a well-localized X-ray transient with refined timing and a preliminary hard spectrum; its physical class remains open.

#### GRB 261113B: an off-axis SVOM/GRM spectrum strengthens the burst classification

SVOM/GRM reported on **17 November at 06:14 UTC** its ground analysis of the event at **2026-11-13 19:45:55.250 UTC**, also recorded by Fermi/GBM and Insight-HXMT. GRM finds a multi-pulsed signal with **T90 = 10.5⁺¹·⁵₋₂·⁵ s** in 15–5000 keV. A power-law fit from T0−7.75 to T0+4.25 s gives photon index **−2.09⁺⁰·¹⁵₋₀·¹¹** and 10–1000 keV fluence **9.09⁺¹·⁰⁹₋₁·⁰⁷ × 10⁻⁶ erg cm⁻²**. [SVOM/GRM analysis](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46311); [Fermi localization](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46281).

The GWAC position is **RA 164.7397862°, Dec +43.9302714°**, with a quoted **0.5-arcsec statistical uncertainty**, but it was **131° from the SVOM optical axis**, outside the ECLAIRs field of view. The GRM team notes that Earth-atmosphere reflection may have contributed to the detection geometry. The calibrated prompt spectrum reinforces the interpretation of the event as a GRB after Fermi's initial particle-event classification, while the unusual off-axis response remains a systematic limitation.

#### GRB 261108D: refined ECLAIRs data favor a soft, low-energy X-ray-flash interpretation

For the burst at **2026-11-08 23:52:36 UTC**, SVOM/ECLAIRs reported on **17 November at 13:50 UTC** a single prompt peak with **T90 = 10.6⁺³·⁶₋₃·³ s** in 4–120 keV. A power-law fit gives index **−2.01⁺⁰·¹⁶₋₀·¹⁹**, fluence **(2.9 ± 0.5) × 10⁻⁷ erg cm⁻²**, and photon flux **1.2 ± 0.1 ph cm⁻² s⁻¹**. A constrained Band fit, with low- and high-energy slopes fixed at −1 and −2.5, gives **Epeak = 19.3⁺⁸·¹₋₅·⁵ keV**. All quoted intervals are 68%. [Refined ECLAIRs analysis](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46313).

This low peak energy motivates the team's X-ray-flash description, but it depends on a spectral model whose slopes were fixed because the data do not determine them. If the tentative **z = 0.6** candidate is the true counterpart, the stated Planck-like cosmology gives **Eiso = 4.0⁺⁰·⁶₋₀·⁵ × 10⁵⁰ erg** and rest-frame **Ep,z = 31⁺¹³₋₉ keV**, placing the event near the low-energy end of the Type-II Amati relation. Those rest-frame quantities are conditional on an unconfirmed redshift and should not be treated as secure energetics.

#### GRB 261108C: ECLAIRs quantifies the broad prompt episode

SVOM/ECLAIRs issued a refined analysis on **17 November at 14:23 UTC** of the burst triggered at **2026-11-08 21:19:10.594 UTC**. The 4–120 keV light curve has a broad structure with **T90 = 83⁺¹³₋₉ s**. Over T0−49 to T0+19 s, before the spacecraft slew, a power law with photon index **−1.87 ± 0.11** gives fluence **(8.3 ± 0.8) × 10⁻⁷ erg cm⁻²** and photon flux **(4.7 ± 0.3) × 10⁻¹ ph cm⁻² s⁻¹**; uncertainties are 68%. [Refined ECLAIRs analysis](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46314).

The refined duration and spectrum establish a long, comparatively soft prompt episode. They do not supply a redshift or bolometric energy, and the fit covers only the pre-slew interval. The result therefore improves the prompt characterization without determining the progenitor environment or intrinsic energetics.

#### Fermi/GBM: two broad candidate localizations await confirmation and tighter follow-up

Fermi/GBM trigger **816645341** occurred on **17 November at 21:55:36.47 UTC**. The onboard classifier assigned **66% probability to a GRB** and **29% to distant particles**; the final public localization is **RA 94.320°, Dec +41.660°**, with a **10.83° statistical uncertainty**. MASTER-SAAO began imaging at **22:34:59 UTC**, about 39 min after the trigger, under a high zenith distance of 78° and reached clear-band limits as deep as **17.4 mag**. It reported no new optical transient. [MASTER follow-up](https://gcn.nasa.gov/circulars/46315); [Fermi trigger table](https://gcn.gsfc.nasa.gov/gcn/fermi_grbs.html). The shallow, very wide-area follow-up does not exclude an optical counterpart.

A second GBM trigger, **816659441**, occurred on **18 November at 01:50:36.86 UTC**. The onboard classifier assigned **79% probability to a GRB** and **19% to Cyg X-1**. Its final public position is **RA 272.230°, Dec +60.710°**, with a **14.72° statistical uncertainty**; the flight trigger had **4.7σ** significance over 4.096 s in 47–291 keV. [Fermi/GBM notices](https://gcn.gsfc.nasa.gov/gcn/fermi_grbs.html). No confirming Circular or narrower counterpart localization was available by the cutoff. Both events remain candidate gamma-ray transients: the classifier probabilities and trigger significances are not astrophysical detection significances, and neither event should yet be named as a confirmed source association.
